MIZORAM PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
COMPETITIVE EXAMINATION FOR RECRUITMENT TO THE POST OF
CIRCLE OFFICER UNDER SOCIAL WELFARE, WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT, GOVERNMENT OF MIZORAM.
(APRIL-2026)
QUESTION BOOKLET
PAPER- I
Time Allowed : 3 hours
Maximum Marks : 100
INSTRUCTIONS
1. Immediately after the commencement of the examination, you should check that this question booklet does
not have any unprinted or torn or missing pages or items, etc.  If so, get it replaced by a complete question
booklet of the same series.
2. Write and encode clearly the question booklet series A or B as the case may be in the space provided in
the OMR Answer Sheet.
3. Particulars/Details to be filled up in the Answer Bookelet and OMR Answer Sheet should be
filled up completely and correctly, OMR Answer Sheet of candidates failing to do so will NOT be
evaluated.
4. This Question Booklet contains Part - ‘A’  & ‘B’. Part - ‘A’ should be answered only on the Answer
Booklet provided  and Part - ‘B’ should be answered only on the OMR Response Sheet .
5. For Part - ‘B’ section you have to mark all your responses only on the separate OMR Response Sheet
provided.  See directions in the OMR Answer Sheet.
6. After the examination has concluded, you should hand over the OMR, Answer Booklet and rough sheet to
the Invigilator only.  You are permitted to take away with you only the Question Booklet.
7. Separate sheets for rough work will be provided in the Examination Hall.
8. There shall be negative marking for all Objective/MCQ type questions
9. For each incorrect answer in the MCQ, one-third (l/3rd) of the marks assigned to that question will be
deducted.

PART- A
(Conventional Type - 40  Marks)
This Section should be answered only on the Answer Booklet provided.
Marks for each question is indicated against it. Attempt all questions.
1. Write an essay choosing one of the topics given below:
(10)
(a) The role of NGOs in community development.
(b) Minimum Government, Maximum Governance
(c) Challenges faced by working women in modern society.
2. Write a precis of the following passage in  about one-third of the words content. Give a suitable title.
(10)
The rapid pace of urbanisation in the modern era has created a significant imbalance between
the city and the countryside. While cities are often viewed as engines of economic growth and hubs of
innovation, they are increasingly becoming overcrowded, leading to a decline in the quality of life.
This phenomenon is largely driven by the lack of opportunities in rural areas, forcing the youth to
migrate in search of better livelihoods. However, a sustainable future for the nation does not lie in the
endless expansion of urban borders, but in the holistic development of our villages.
True progress can only be achieved when rural areas are equipped with modern infrastructure,
quality education, and accessible healthcare. If we can provide the same digital and physical connectivity
in villages that is currently exclusive to cities, we can curb forced migration. Furthermore, empowering
rural industries and agriculture through technology will create local employment, reducing the burden
on urban resources. The goal should not be to turn every village into a city, but to provide urban-like
amenities in a rural setting. Only by bridging this developmental gap can we ensure balanced national
growth and prevent our cities from collapsing under the weight of their own population.
3. Write a Letter to the Mayor of Aizawl Municipal Corporation highlighting the rising incidence of
burglary in various localities of Aizawl city and urging him to implement concrete measures to address
the issue, including some remedial suggestions. Sign as XYZ of ABC locality.
(10)
4. Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.
In the contemporary digital era, social media has emerged as a dominant force shaping the
lives of young individuals. While it provides unprecedented opportunities for communication, self-
expression, and access to information, its pervasive influence has raised serious concerns regarding
youth mental health. The constant exposure to curated and idealized representations of life often
leads to unhealthy comparisons, fostering feelings of inadequacy, low self-esteem, and anxiety among
adolescents.
Moreover, the addictive nature of social media platforms exacerbates these issues. The
pursuit of validation through likes, comments, and followers can create a cycle of dependency, where
self-worth becomes contingent upon virtual approval. This phenomenon not only distracts young
people from real-life interactions but also contributes to social isolation and emotional distress. Studies
have shown that excessive screen time is closely associated with sleep disturbances, reduced
concentration, and increased levels of stress.
Another critical aspect is the prevalence of cyberbullying, which has become a significant
threat in the digital landscape. Unlike traditional forms of bullying, online harassment can be relentless
and far-reaching, leaving victims with little respite. The anonymity afforded by social media often
emboldens perpetrators, intensifying the psychological impact on victims and, in severe cases, leading
to depression and suicidal tendencies.
However, it is important to acknowledge that social media is not inherently detrimental.
When used responsibly, it can serve as a platform for awareness, support, and community building.

- 3 -
Series - A
Mental health campaigns, peer support groups, and access to professional resources have become
more accessible through digital channels.
In conclusion, while social media offers numerous benefits, its adverse effects on youth
mental health cannot be overlooked. A balanced approach involving digital literacy, parental guidance,
and self-regulation is essential to mitigate its negative consequences and promote overall well-being.
Answer the following questions below:
(a) What are the positive aspects of social media mentioned in the passage?
(2)
(b) How does social media contribute to low self-esteem among youth?
(2)
(c) Why does anonymity increase the severity of cyberbullying?
(2)
(d) What measures are suggested to reduce the negative impact of social media?
(2)
(e) In the sentence: “The constant exposure to curated and idealized representations of life
often leads to unhealthy comparisions…”
Choose the word closest in meaning to “curated” in this context:
(1)
(a) Random
(b) Carefully selected
(c) Overlooked
(d) Haphazard
(f) In the sentence: “It is important to acknowledge that social media is not inherently
detrimental…”
Choose the word most opposite in meaning to “inherently” in the context of the passage:
(1)
(a) Naturally
(b) Intrinsically
(c) Incidentally
(d) Fundamentally
PART- B

All questions carry equal mark of 1 each. Attempt all questions.
This Section should be answered only on the OMR Response Sheet provided.

(b) Adverb

(b) Adverb

Direction (Question Nos. 11 - 20): Fill in the blanks with suitable prepositions from the alternatives

(b) at
(c) on
(d) in

(a) in
(b) to
(c) into
(d) of
13. You do not need to get up because the phone is lying _______ hand.
(a) at
(b) in
(c) on
(d) from
14. There is no limit _______ the wants of man.

(b) to
(c) in
(d) of
15. The team was elated with joy _______ their victory.

(b) to
(c) from
(d) over
16. He talks _______ his father.

(b) as
(c) from
(d) at

19. Abiding _______law is the culture of civilized nations.

Series - A
20. India is committed _______ a policy of peaceful existence.

(b) to

Direction (Question Nos. 41 - 50): Choose the most appropriate type of  Clause/Speech from the
alternatives given:
41. The manager asked us if we could finish the project by Monday.
(a) Adjective clause
(b) Adverb clause
(c) Noun clause
(d) Conditional clause
42. We left the park early because it started raining.
(a) Adjective clause
(b) Adverb clause
(c) Noun clause
(d) Conditional clause
43. The painting which was stolen yesterday has been recovered.
(a) Adjective clause
(b) Adverb clause
(c) Noun clause
(d) Conditional clause
44. She was late as she missed the bus.
(a) Adjective clause
(b) Adverb clause
(c) Noun clause
(d) Conditional clause

- 7 -
Series - A
45. I like the house whose garden is full of flowers.
(a) Conditional clause
(b) Adverb clause
(c) Noun clause
(d) Adjective clause
46. “We will help you tomorrow,” they said.
(a) They said that they will help me tomorrow.
(b) They said that they would help me the next day.
(c) They said that they would help you tomorrow.
(d) They said that they help me tomorrow.
47. “I can finish this work by evening,” he said.
(a) He said that he could finish that work by evening.
(b) He said that he can finish this work by evening.
(c) He said that he could finish that work by that evening.
(d) He said that he could finish this work by that evening.
48. “I shall never forget this day,” she said.
(a) She said that she shall never forget that day.
(b) She said that she would never forget that day.
(c) She said she will never forget this day.
(d) She said that she would never forget this day.
49. He said that he must submit the report the next day.
(a) He said, “I must submit the report tomorrow.”
(b) He said, “I must submit the report the next day.”
(c) He said, “I have to submit the report tomorrow.”
(d) He said, “I should submit the report tomorrow.”
50. He said that he would help me the next day.
(a) He said, “I will help you the next day.”
(b) He said, “I would help you tomorrow.”
(c) He said, “I will help you tomorrow.”
(d) He said, “I would help you the next day.”
Direction (Question Nos. 51 - 60): Choose the correct answer from the alternatives for the following
questions as directed:
51. She sings very well. (Change into interrogative)
(a) Does she sing very well?
(b) How well does she sing?
(c) She sings well?
(d) She sings very well, right?
52. Hardly had he reached the station when the train left. (Change into affirmative)
(a) He reached the station before the train left.
(b) He had reached the station when the train left.
(c) The train left after he reached the station.
(d) He reached the station just as the train left.
53. Hardly had he finished his work when the boss called him again. (Change into interrogative)
(a) Had he hardly finished his work when the boss called him?
(b) Did he finish his work before the boss called?
(c) Had he finished his work when the boss called him?
(d) Was the boss calling him while he finished?

- 8 -
Series - A
54. The exam was so tough that many students failed. (Change into exclamatory)
(a) How tough the exam was!
(b) Exam was tough!
(c) Many students failed the exam!
(d) The exam was tough!
55. She always speaks the truth. (Change into negative)
(a) She never speaks the truth.
(b) She hardly ever speaks the truth.
(c) She does not always speak the truth.
(d) She rarely speaks the truth.
56. The dog barked loudly, and the cat ran away. (Change into simple sentence)
(a) Hearing the dog bark loudly, the cat ran away.
(b) The dog barked loudly, so the cat ran away.
(c) Although the dog barked loudly, the cat ran away.
(d) The dog barked loudly; the cat ran away.
57. I was hungry. I did not eat lunch. (Change into complex sentence)
(a) I was hungry, and I did not eat lunch.
(b) I was hungry, but I did not eat lunch.
(c) I was hungry, so I did not eat lunch.
(d) Although I was hungry, I did not eat lunch.
58. It rained heavily. The match was postponed. (Change into compound sentence)
(a) Because it rained heavily, the match was postponed.
(b) It rained heavily, so the match was postponed.
(c) Although it rained heavily, the match was postponed.
(d) It rained heavily and the match was postponed.
59. Me and my brother went to the market. (Correct the sentence)
(a) Me and my brother went to the market.
(b) My brother and me went to the market.
(c) My brother and I went to the market.
(d) I and my brother went to the market.
60. “I suggested him to apply for the job.” (Correct the sentence)
(a) I suggested him to apply for the job.
(b) I suggested that he applies for the job.
(c) I suggested that he apply for the job.
(d) I suggested him applying for the job.
